why: Create a page and change another: the common case
description:
Add a page at /about with the heading "About us" and one short paragraph about the team.

Acceptance criteria:
- Visiting /about shows the heading "About us"
- The /about page has one paragraph of text below the heading
- The home page has a link to /about

why: Change the shared layout, not every page
description:
Add a site footer that appears on every page.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every page shows a footer with the text "© 2026 Agent Playground"
- The footer has a link with the text "Home" that goes to /
- The footer is part of the shared layout, so new pages get it automatically

why: A one-line change: should be cheap and fast
description:
Change the home page heading to "Welcome to Agent Playground".

Acceptance criteria:
- The home page heading reads "Welcome to Agent Playground"
- The old text "Hello from the starter app" no longer appears

why: A client component with state: needs real thinking
summary: Add a like button to the home page
description:
Add a "Like" button to the home page that counts clicks.

Acceptance criteria:
- The home page shows a button with the text "Like (0)"
- Each click adds one: after two clicks it reads "Like (2)"
- The count resets when the page is reloaded (no saving)

why: Must stop at the reader with questions, almost free
description: The site should look better and be more modern.

why: Must stop at the planner: the app has no login system to extend
summary: Show the user's name in the header
description:
Use the existing login system to show the logged-in user's name in the header.

Acceptance criteria:
- A logged-in user sees "Hi, <name>" in the header
- A visitor who is not logged in sees a "Log in" link instead

why: Backend + frontend with a contract: routing should pick the strong reviewer
summary: Add a contact form with a server endpoint
description:
Add a contact page with a form that sends messages to a new server endpoint.

Acceptance criteria:
- /contact shows a form with name, email and message fields and a Send button
- Submitting posts the form as JSON to POST /api/contact
- POST /api/contact returns 400 with {"error": "Email is required"} when email is missing or empty
- POST /api/contact returns 200 with {"ok": true} for a valid message
- After a successful send, the page shows "Thanks, we'll be in touch" instead of the form
- After a 400, the page shows the error message and keeps the form

why: Many criteria: routing should pick the strong planner
description:
Add a todo list at /todos that keeps items in the browser.

Acceptance criteria:
- /todos shows a text box and an Add button
- Adding a non-empty item shows it in the list; empty input adds nothing
- Each item has a checkbox; checking it marks the item done (line-through)
- Each item has a Delete button that removes it
- The page shows "N left" counting items not done
- With no items, the page shows "Nothing to do"
- Items survive a page reload (stored in localStorage)

why: A refactor: change structure without changing behaviour
summary: Extract a reusable page heading component
description:
Pages each style their own h1. Make one PageHeading component and use it.

Acceptance criteria:
- A PageHeading component renders an h1 with the existing heading style (text-2xl font-semibold)
- The home page uses PageHeading instead of its own h1
- The home page looks and reads exactly as before (same heading text)

why: Backend only: a route handler and its tests
description:
Add GET /api/health for uptime monitors.

Acceptance criteria:
- GET /api/health returns status 200
- The body is JSON {"status": "ok"}
- The response has the header Cache-Control: no-store

why: Client state + browser API + layout: easy to get subtly wrong
description:
Add a button that switches the site between light and dark.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every page shows a "Dark mode" button in the top right
- Clicking it adds the class "dark" to the html element and the button then reads "Light mode"
- Clicking again removes the class and the button reads "Dark mode" again
- The choice survives a page reload (stored in localStorage)
